whole_task_scope:
## R2. Writer convergence
The accepted whole Task requires all current writers of the eligibility set to apply the corrected per-account uniqueness rule. This includes legacy_writer.py. D1 delivered only the new writer and changed the decision text; a planned later Delivery within this same Task owns the legacy writer adaptation and switch. The later Delivery has no implementation or delivered result yet. It is not an external-evidence-only requirement. Independent export search and privacy paths below are outside this migration scope.

## R3. Assess other existing adopters
Completion also evaluates the two other existing-adopter arrangements described in docs/migration-facts.md. For catalog-search, assess the relation to the corrected writer state, the effects of coexistence and remaining consumers, the stated retention grounds, the responsible owner, the executable successor or observable migration trigger, and the evidence for exit. For confidential export, assess the actual scenario and whether its existing protection still has a current basis. Explain the evidence supporting each disposition and any unresolved gap; no disposition is prescribed by this requirement. This assessment belongs to the current Task. Implementing or switching either of these two other paths remains outside this Task, and their assessment does not discharge the unfinished R2 writer migration.

# Actual decision and implementation facts
The decision text now describes one per-account eligibility row. The new writer uses account keys; the old writer still overwrites the same shared eligibility collection under a global singleton key. Both paths are active for the same accounts; new entry availability and CURRENT promotion have been observed, old migration and environment switch have not.
An independent catalog-search legacy cursor uses a separate key and dataset, with no eligibility-state dependency. Search owner will migrate it in the named search D2 when its existing client window closes; the observable trigger is zero old-version clients for the documented support interval. Exit evidence is all registered search callers on the new codec and no reads of the old key. During that period its old client contract and account/query checks remain valid; new search consumers use the target codec. This work is outside this Task scope.
A confidential export still has a current bearer confidentiality contract and uses the existing export key. It is a different scenario and not a retired search dependency.
These are fixture operation facts and planned work, not Completion conclusions. No cloud or production write was run.
